text:
maria: seeing ~18 targets on alb-edge-us-west-2 get marked unhealthy and deregistered at 2025-11-12T14:12:01Z. No canary deploys running AFAIK. Anyone else?
ken: wow, that's a lot. Do we have correlation with node events or egress IP churn?
maria: checking. kube events show a burst of pod ip rotations on edge-nodes-autoscale group around 14:11.
oliver: I see the ALB logs show repeated 502/504 health checks coming from a handful of ephemeral source IPs. Looks like health check source IP changed mid-window.
anya: could this be the VPC NAT scaling we rolled yesterday? NAT gateway autoscale might rotate source IPs for SNAT.
maria: timeline: 14:08 scale up start, 14:11 pod IPs reallocated (kube-proxy reports), 14:12 ALB starts deregistering targets.
ken: repro steps? can you paste the half of ALB log around 14:12?
oliver: paste: ```ALB 2025-11-12T14:12:01Z request: client=10.2.1.5:3456 target=10.0.120.45:8080 elb-status=504 target-status=504 "GET /healthz HTTP/1.1"```
maria: and then after ip rotation: ```ALB 2025-11-12T14:12:07Z request: client=10.2.1.7:3456 target=10.0.121.12:8080 elb-status=502 target-status=502"GET /healthz HTTP/1.1"```
anya: those elb client IPs look like SNATed egress pool addresses. If LB health checks are being sourced from different IPs and we have an ip-based allowlist on sidecars, healthcheck hits could be rejected.
ken: sidecar? we have a network policy plus iptables rules on the envoy sidecar that only allow ALB healthcheck CIDRs we recorded at deploy time. If source IP changes, it will drop.
maria: confirmed: envoy logs show 403 from ip-restrictor for inbound health probes when the SNAT pool changed. Example: ```2025-11-12T14:12:06Z envoy warn: inbound healthcheck denied src=10.2.1.7:3456 rule=allowlist-alb-ips```
oliver: that would explain immediate target deregistration. ALB marks target unhealthy after consecutive failed checks (we're at threshold 2).
anya: hmm. we assumed NAT source IPs were stable per region. But with NAT autoscaler + shared egress, they rotate ephemeral addresses. Need to move to healthchecks that don't rely on client IP allowlist.
ken: quick mitigation: can we relax sidecar allowlist to accept the whole NAT pool CIDR? Risky but temporary.
maria: alternative: use ALB healthcheck source cidrs (aws docs) vs our nat pool. But ALB uses the subnets' addresses as client IPs for healthchecks when probing from within VPC? Not always, see notes.
oliver: immediate action: adding the NAT egress pool CIDR to the allowlist on edge sidecars and rolling config on edge-daemonset. Low blast? should be fine for 10m window.
anya: file a followup to make health check logic based on Host header path + mutual TLS for probe endpoints so we don't rely on source IPs.
ken: agree. Also add alert for "ALB healthcheck client IP changes" to catch this earlier.
maria: I'm going to roll the allowlist change now. rolling patch: ```kubectl set env ds/edge-sidecar ALLOW_HEALTHCHECK_CIDRS=10.2.0.0/18 --namespace edge-system```
anya: heads up: that env is picked up by the ip-restrictor on restart; we might need a quick restart of daemonset pods.
maria: triggering restart: ```kubectl rollout restart ds/edge-sidecar -n edge-system```
ken: can you monitor targets? I'll watch ALB target group.
maria: update 14:18: after restart, ALB healthchecks started succeeding and targets re-registered over ~90s. Back to normal. :tada:
oliver: great. Postmortem items: 1) don't use client IP allowlist for LB healthchecks 2) document NAT autoscaling semantics and how it affects probe IP stability 3) add metric for consecutive target deregisters in a region.
anya: also consider using NodePort + internal NLB healthchecks that originate from stable ENI addresses or use cross-zone healthchecks.
ken: cost note: widening allowlist to CIDR is quick but expands attack surface for that endpoint; make sure auth is required on /healthz and we rate-limit.
maria: will open a ticket with proposed long-term fixes and an ETA. Thanks everyone.

maria: filing: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2678 - will add logs and timeline.
anya: nice triage. I'm going to draft the postmortem template with action items.
ken: adding a followup to infra runbook for NAT changes.
maria: closing thread for now, will post PM when ticket has remediation plan. :white_check_mark:"
